Under `[profile.<name>.lint.lint_specific]`, `mixed_case_exceptions` lists
allowed mixed-case name fragments and `multi_contract_file_exceptions` accepts
`interface`, `library`, and `abstract_contract`.

## In-line test configuration

Foundry users are enabled to specify overall test configurations, using a combination of ENV variables and config statements in the `foundry.toml`. Checkout the [`Testing reference`][Testing Reference] for a detailed description.

Despite this may work in the general case, some tests may need finer control over their configuration. For such reason Forge provides a way to specify per-test configs for invariant and fuzz testing scenarios.

Users can in-line test config statements directly in Solidity comments. This would affect the behavior of the `forge test` command for a specific test instance, as illustrated in the example below.

```solidity
contract MyTest is Test {
  /// forge-config: default.fuzz.runs = 100
  /// forge-config: ci.fuzz.runs = 500
  /// forge-config: default.fuzz.show-logs = true
  function test_SimpleFuzzTest(uint256 x) public {
    // --- snip ---
  }
}
```

What we are asking here is to run our fuzzer `100` and `500` times for the `default` and `ci` profiles respectively. The interesting fact is that this would override any fuzz `runs` setup existing at a global level. All other configs would be inherited from the global context, making this acting as a fallback for all possible configurations.

### Block comments

In-line test configurations can also be expressed in block comments, as illustrated in the example.

```solidity
contract MyTest is Test {
  /**
   * forge-config: default.fuzz.runs = 1024
   * forge-config: default.fuzz.max-test-rejects = 500
   * forge-config: default.fuzz.show-logs = true
   */
  function test_SimpleFuzzTest(uint256 x) public {
    // --- snip ---
  }
}
```

### In-line fuzz configs

Users can specify the configs described in the table. Each statement must have a prefix of the form `forge-config: ${PROFILE}.fuzz.`

| Parameter          | Type    | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `runs`             | integer | The amount of fuzz runs to perform for this specific test case. [`Reference`][testing].                                              |
| `max-test-rejects` | integer | The maximum number of combined inputs that may be rejected before the test as a whole aborts. [`Reference`][Max test rejects].       |
| `show-logs`        | boolean | The flag indicates whether to display console logs in fuzz tests or not. Works when `verbosity >= 2`. [`Reference`][Fuzz show logs]. |

Fuzz config example

```solidity
contract MyFuzzTest is Test {
  /// forge-config: default.fuzz.runs = 100
  /// forge-config: default.fuzz.max-test-rejects = 2
  /// forge-config: default.fuzz.show-logs = true
  function test_InlineConfig(uint256 x) public {
    // --- snip ---
  }
}
```

### In-line invariant configs

Users can specify the configs described in the table. Each statement must have a prefix of the form `forge-config: ${PROFILE}.invariant.`

| Parameter        | Type    | Description                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `runs`           | integer | The amount of invariant runs to perform for this specific test case. [`Reference`][Invariant runs].    |
| `depth`          | integer | The number of calls executed to attempt to break invariant in one run. [`Reference`][Invariant depth]. |
| `fail-on-revert` | boolean | Fails the invariant fuzzing if a revert occurs. [`Reference`][Fail on revert].                         |
| `call-override`  | boolean | Overrides unsafe external calls when running invariant test. [`Reference`][Invariant call override].   |

Invariant config example

```solidity
contract MyInvariantTest is Test {
  /// forge-config: default.invariant.runs = 100
  /// forge-config: default.invariant.depth = 2
  /// forge-config: default.invariant.fail-on-revert = false
  /// forge-config: default.invariant.call-override = true
  function invariant_InlineConfig() public {
    // --- snip ---
  }
}
```

[Testing Reference]: ./testing

[testing]: ./testing#runs

[Max test rejects]: ./testing#max_test_rejects

[Fuzz show logs]: ./testing#show_logs

[Invariant runs]: ./testing#runs-1

[Invariant depth]: ./testing#depth

[Fail on revert]: ./testing#fail_on_revert

## Formatter

Configuration related to the behavior of the Forge formatter. Each of these keys live under the `[fmt]` section.

### `line_length`

* Type: number
* Default: 120
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_LINE_LENGTH` or `DAPP_FMT_LINE_LENGTH`

Maximum line length where formatter will try to wrap the line.

### `tab_width`

* Type: number
* Default: 4
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_TAB_WIDTH` or `DAPP_FMT_TAB_WIDTH`

Number of spaces per indentation level. Ignored if `style` is set to `"tab"`.

### `style`

* Type: string
* Default: `space`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_STYLE` or `DAPP_FMT_STYLE`

Indentation style. Valid values are:

* `space` (default): Use spaces for indentation
* `tab`: Use tabs for indentation

### `bracket_spacing`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_BRACKET_SPACING` or `DAPP_FMT_BRACKET_SPACING`

Whether or not to print spaces between brackets.

### `int_types`

* Type: string
* Default: `long`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_INT_TYPES` or `DAPP_FMT_INT_TYPES`

Style of uint/int256 types. Valid values are:

* `long` (default): Use the explicit `uint256` or `int256`
* `short`: Use the implicit `uint` or `int`
* `preserve`: Use the type defined in the source code

### `multiline_func_header`

* Type: string
* Default: `attributes_first`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_MULTILINE_FUNC_HEADER` or `DAPP_FMT_MULTILINE_FUNC_HEADER`

Style of multiline function header in case it doesn't fit in one line. Valid values are:

* `attributes_first` (default): Write function attributes multiline first
* `params_always`: Always write function parameters multiline
* `params_first_multi`: Write function parameters multiline first when there is more than one param
* `all`: If function params or attrs are multiline, multiline everything
* `all_params`: Same as `all` but writes function params multiline even when there is a single param

For example, with `params_always`:

```solidity
function myFunction(
    uint256 param1,
    uint256 param2,
    uint256 param3
) public returns (uint256) {
  // ...
}
```

And with `all`:

```solidity
function myFunction(
    uint256 param1,
    uint256 param2,
    uint256 param3
)
    public
    returns (uint256)
{
  // ...
}
```

### `quote_style`

* Type: string
* Default: `double`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_QUOTE_STYLE` or `DAPP_FMT_QUOTE_STYLE`

Defines the quotation mark style. Valid values are:

* `double` (default): Use double quotes where possible (`"`)
* `single`: Use single quotes where possible (`'`)
* `preserve`: Use quotation mark defined in the source code

### `number_underscore`

* Type: string
* Default: `preserve`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_NUMBER_UNDERSCORE` or `DAPP_FMT_NUMBER_UNDERSCORE`

Style of underscores in number literals. Valid values are:

* `preserve` (default): Use the underscores defined in the source code
* `thousands`: Add an underscore every thousand, if greater than 9999. i.e. `1000` is formatted as `1000` and `10000` as `10_000`
* `remove`: Remove all underscores

### `hex_underscore`

* Type: string
* Default: `remove`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_HEX_UNDERSCORE` or `DAPP_FMT_HEX_UNDERSCORE`

Style of underscores in hex literals. Valid values are:

* `preserve`: Use the underscores defined in the source code
* `remove` (default): Remove all underscores
* `bytes`: Add underscore as separator between byte boundaries. i.e. `hex"deadbeef"` is formatted as `hex"de_ad_be_ef"`

### `single_line_statement_blocks`

* Type: string
* Default: `preserve`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_SINGLE_LINE_STATEMENT_BLOCKS` or `DAPP_FMT_SINGLE_LINE_STATEMENT_BLOCKS`

Style of single line blocks in statements. Valid values are:

* `preserve` (default): Keep the existing single/multi line formatting of statement blocks
* `single`: Statement blocks will be formatted to a single line if possible
* `multi`: Statement blocks will always be formatted to multiple lines

For example, with `single`:

```solidity
if (true) { return true; }
```

With `multi`:

```solidity
if (true) {
    return true;
}
```

### `override_spacing`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_OVERRIDE_SPACING` or `DAPP_FMT_OVERRIDE_SPACING`

Whether to print a space in state variable, function and modifier `override` attribute.

When enabled:

```solidity
function foo() override (Parent) public { }
```

When disabled:

```solidity
function foo() override(Parent) public { }
```

### `wrap_comments`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_WRAP_COMMENTS` or `DAPP_FMT_WRAP_COMMENTS`

Whether or not to wrap comments on `line_length` reached.

### `docs_style`

* Type: string
* Default: `preserve`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_DOCS_STYLE` or `DAPP_FMT_DOCS_STYLE`

Style of doc comments. Valid values are:

* `preserve` (default): Preserve the source code style
* `line`: Use single-line style (`///`)
* `block`: Use block style (`/** ... */`)

### `ignore`

* Type: array of strings (patterns)
* Default: `[]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_IGNORE` or `DAPP_FMT_IGNORE`

List of files to ignore when formatting. This is a comma separated list of glob patterns.

```toml
[fmt]
ignore = ["src/vendor/**/*.sol", "lib/**/*.sol"]
```

### `contract_new_lines`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_CONTRACT_NEW_LINES` or `DAPP_FMT_CONTRACT_NEW_LINES`

Whether to add new lines before and after contract declarations.

When enabled:

```solidity
// imports...

contract MyContract {
    // ...
}

contract AnotherContract {
    // ...
}
```

### `sort_imports`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_SORT_IMPORTS` or `DAPP_FMT_SORT_IMPORTS`

Whether to sort import statements alphabetically within their import groups. Groups are separated by blank lines.

### `namespace_import_style`

* Type: string
* Default: `prefer_plain`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_NAMESPACE_IMPORT_STYLE` or `DAPP_FMT_NAMESPACE_IMPORT_STYLE`

Choose between import styles. Valid values are:

* `prefer_plain` (default): Prefer `import "source" as name;`
* `prefer_glob`: Prefer `import * as name from "source";`
* `preserve`: Preserve the original style

### `pow_no_space`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_POW_NO_SPACE` or `DAPP_FMT_POW_NO_SPACE`

Whether to suppress spaces around the power operator (`**`).

When enabled:

```solidity
uint256 result = base**exponent;
```

When disabled (default):

```solidity
uint256 result = base ** exponent;
```

### `prefer_compact`

* Type: string
* Default: `all`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_PREFER_COMPACT` or `DAPP_FMT_PREFER_COMPACT`

Style that determines if a broken list should keep its elements together on their own line, before breaking individually. Valid values are:

* `all` (default): All elements are preferred compact
* `none`: All elements are preferred consistent
* `calls`: Calls are preferred compact; events and errors break consistently
* `events`: Events are preferred compact; calls and errors break consistently
* `errors`: Errors are preferred compact; calls and events break consistently
* `events_errors`: Events and errors are preferred compact; calls break consistently

### `single_line_imports`

* Type: bool
* Default: false
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_FMT_SINGLE_LINE_IMPORTS` or `DAPP_FMT_SINGLE_LINE_IMPORTS`

Keep single imports on a single line even if they exceed `line_length`.

## Linter Configuration

Configuration related to the behavior of the linter. These keys are set in the `[lint]` section.

##### `lint_on_build`

* Type: boolean
* Default: `true`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_LINT_ON_BUILD`

Whether to run linting during `forge build`. Set to `false` to disable automatic linting during builds.

##### `severity`

* Type: array of strings
* Default: `["high", "medium", "low"]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_LINT_SEVERITY`

Specifies which lints to run based on severity. Valid values are:

* `high`
* `medium` (or `med`)
* `low`
* `info`
* `gas`
* `code-size` (or `codesize`, `size`)

By default, Forge runs high, medium, and low severity lints. An empty list means no severity filter
is applied, enabling all severity buckets, including informational, gas, and code-size lints.

##### `exclude_lints`

* Type: array of strings
* Default: `[]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_LINT_EXCLUDE_LINTS`

List of lint IDs to exclude from checking (e.g., `"mixed-case-function"`).

##### `ignore`

* Type: array of strings (patterns)
* Default: `[]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_LINT_IGNORE`

List of files or patterns to ignore when running the linter. This is a comma-separated list of glob patterns.

##### `mixed_case_exceptions`

* Type: array of strings
* Default: `["ERC", "URI", "ID", "URL", "API", "JSON", "XML", "HTML", "HTTP", "HTTPS"]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_LINT_MIXED_CASE_EXCEPTIONS`

Configurable patterns that should be excluded when performing `mixedCase` and `PascalCase` lint checks. The defaults allow common names like `rescueERC20`, `ERC721TokenReceiver`, `tokenURI`, or `ERC20Data`.

## Inline Configuration

The linter also offers the ability to disable lints for specific sections of code using inline comment directives.
This is useful when you need to suppress false positives or have valid reasons for code that would otherwise trigger a lint warning.

To disable lints using inline config, your comment must follow this format:

```
/// forge-lint: <directive>(<lint-ids>)
```

Where:

* `<directive>` is one of the directives from the table below
* `<lint-ids>` is a comma-separated list of lint identifiers, or `all` to disable all lints

### Supported Inline Directives

| Directive                       | Description                                                                        | Scope                              |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `disable-next-item`             | Disables lints for the next code item (contract, function, variable, struct, etc.) | Next item regardless of line count |
| `disable-line`                  | Disables lints for the current line                                                | Current line only                  |
| `disable-next-line`             | Disables lints for the next line                                                   | Next line only                     |
| `disable-start` / `disable-end` | Disables lints for all code between the start and end comments                     | Block of code between directives   |

### Best Practices

1. **Be Specific**: Always specify which lint(s) you're disabling rather than using `all`.
2. **Add Comments**: Explain why you're disabling the lint to help future maintainers.
3. **Minimize Scope**: Use the most targeted directive possible (e.g., `disable-line` instead of `disable-start/end`).

### Disabling Linter On Build

By default, the linter runs automatically when you build your project with `forge build`.

To skip linting for a single invocation, pass `--no-lint` (alias `--skip-lint`):

```bash
forge build --no-lint
```

To disable persistently, in your `foundry.toml` set:

```toml
[lint]
lint_on_build = false
```

It is however recommended to keep linting enabled during development to catch issues early.
We are continuously improving the linter and you may be missing out on valuable feedback by disabling it.

It is better to configure your `foundry.toml` to only run specific severities by setting the [`severity`](#severity) key, exclude
certain lints with [`exclude_lints`](#exclude_lints), or ignore certain files with [`ignore`](#ignore).

## Documentation Generator

Configuration related to the behavior of the Forge documentation generator. These keys are set in `[doc]` section.

##### `out`

* Type: string
* Default: `docs`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_OUT`

An output path for generated documentation.

##### `title`

* Type: string
* Default: `""`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_TITLE`

Title for the generated documentation.

##### `book`

* Type: string
* Default: `book.toml`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_BOOK`

Legacy configuration key retained for compatibility. `forge doc` now generates a Vocs site and does not read `book.toml`.

##### `homepage`

* Type: string
* Default: `README.md`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_HOMEPAGE`

Path to user provided welcome markdown. If none is provided, it defaults to `README.md`.

##### `repository`

* Type: string
* Default: none
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_REPOSITORY`

The git repository URL. Used to provide links to git source files.
If missing, `forge` will attempt to look up the current origin url and use its value.

##### `commit`

* Type: string
* Default: current Git revision
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_COMMIT`

The Git commit hash, tag, or branch used for source and homepage links.

##### `path`

* Type: string
* Default: none
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_PATH`

Legacy configuration key retained for compatibility. Source links are now derived from the project root and source file path.

##### `ignore`

* Type: array of strings (patterns)
* Default: `[]`
* Environment: `FOUNDRY_DOC_IGNORE`

List of files to ignore when generating documentation. This is a comma separated list of glob patterns.

## Etherscan

Configuration related to Etherscan, such as API keys. This configuration is used in various places by Forge.

The `[etherscan]` section is a mapping of keys to Etherscan configuration tables.

With Etherscan API V2, only Etherscan keys are valid, which can be used to access all similar explorers (e.g. BscScan / BaseScan / Polygonscan).

```toml
[etherscan]
mainnet = { key = "${ETHERSCAN_API_KEY}" }
mainnet2 = { key = "ABCDEFG", chain = "mainnet" }
optimism = { key = "1234567" }
unknown_chain = { key = "ABCDEFG", url = "<etherscan api url for this chain>" }
```

# Changelog

## v1.10.0 (2026-11-19)

Foundry 1.10.0 replaces revm with [evm2](https://github.com/alloy-rs/evm2), a new blazing fast execution engine, across Forge, Anvil, Cast and Chisel. Read **Action required** before upgrading, because gas numbers and some execution details change.

**What you get:**

* **Up to 4.5× faster tests on evm2.** A tighter interpreter, and inspectors that step only the opcodes they act on, make `forge test` 4.5× faster than 1.9.0 on Morpho Blue, 3.5× on Spark PSM and 2.1× on Aave v4.
* **Pinned Solar releases.** `solc = "solar:0.3.0"` pins a Solar release, which Forge downloads if it is missing, and `forge build -j 4` compiles with four Solar threads.
* **Tempo T14 configurable accounts.** Create configurable accounts, manage their owners and thresholds, and send transactions their owners sign, from Cast, Forge and Anvil.
* **Faster debugger.** On the 1.46M-step Aave v4 test, SolDB is ready in 1.40 s instead of 1.96 s, with peak memory around 1 GiB. The opcode pane shows PUSH values again.
* **Deeper invariant campaigns.** Runs resume from states reached by earlier runs, and failing fuzz and invariant tests report minimized counterexamples.
* **About 220 fixes** across symbolic execution, coverage, cheatcodes, fuzzing, Anvil and Cast.

## Action required

* **Gas snapshots (evm2):** regenerate them. Fork warmth and fork transient storage no longer leak from `setUp`, and `vm.setArbitraryStorage` leaves slots cold. A halting call under `vm.expectRevert` now consumes all forwarded gas, as on chain, unless the test makes it directly as a non-static call with `isolate = true`. If later work in the test runs out of gas, forward a fixed amount, as in `target.f{gas: 100_000}()` (#17541, #18396).
* **Remappings:** when a dependency's remapping conflicts with another dependency or a root path, it now applies only inside that dependency, which can change which copy a dependency compiles against. A root import of that alias then fails with an error that suggests the remapping to add, or silently resolves to another target, and Forge warns in that case. Adding the old line to your root remappings restores 1.9 resolution for the whole project (#18433, #18573, #18590, #18603).
* **Test discovery:** only suites under `src`, `test` and `script` run, and `forge test` warns about project suites it skips. Widen `test` to keep running them (#18424, #18572).
* **Invariants:** snapshot fuzzing is on by default, so a run can start from a state an earlier run reached instead of from `setUp`. Handlers and `afterInvariant` hooks that assume a fresh state per run can fail (#18018).

## Performance

* **evm2:** inspectors step only the opcodes they act on and per-call and per-step overhead is trimmed, so `forge test` is 4.5× faster than 1.9.0 on Morpho Blue, 3.5× on Spark PSM and 2.1× on Aave v4 (#17541, #18412, #18476) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @grandizzy, @joshieDo, @emmajam, @pepyakin, @0xKarl98, @figtracer.
* **Debugger:** the Aave v4 session is ready in 1.40 s instead of 1.96 s. The recorder appends only new stack words and no longer uses excessive memory on multi-call transactions such as Tempo batches (#18285, #18392, #18394) by @figtracer, @mablr, @stevencartavia.
* **Invariant campaigns:** predicates run without instrumentation, campaigns drop the tracer, prefixes replay once, and hints and coverage keys are smaller (#18121, #18244, #18166, #18180, #18474, #18243) by @figtracer.
* **Forks, Anvil, gas reports and coverage:** the opt-in `fork_prefetch` also prefetches the state of simulated calls, Anvil fork history shares unchanged state, and gas reports and coverage use less memory (#18247, #18435, #18423, #18129, #18473, #18475) by @figtracer, @mablr, @stevencartavia.
* **Linking, cheatcodes and lints:** library paths are canonicalized only when needed, cheatcodes cache env overrides, and `reentrancy-balance` no longer re-analyzes callees per call site (#18160, #18125, #18063) by @figtracer, @stevencartavia, @DaniPopes.

## Features

### Forge

* **Solar:** `solc = "solar:<version>"`, also accepted by `--use` and `FOUNDRY_SOLC_VERSION`, pins an exact Solar release that Forge downloads and checks. Forge passes its thread count to Solar (#18068, #18092) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @DaniPopes.
* **Invariant and fuzz campaigns:** snapshot fuzzing resumes runs from states with rare storage features, delays come from the fuzz dictionary, and `invariant.call_gas_limit` caps campaign calls. Failing tests report minimized values that still fail the same way, and the dictionary prefers typed samples. The experimental `instrumented_edges` takes coverage from compiler-instrumented builds, which need an unreleased Solar plugin (#18018, #18139, #18227, #18250, #18391, #18195, #18165, #18167, #18179, #18204) by @0xalpharush, @stevencartavia, @mablr, @figtracer.
* **Symbolic execution:** `forge equivalence` checks that two runtime bytecodes behave the same for every input, and the opt-in `--symbolic-live` worker solves branches during invariant campaigns. Added Amsterdam opcodes, `CLZ` and `mulDiv` reasoning (#18065, #18145, #18093, #18091, #18442, #18498) by @0xalpharush, @stevencartavia, @mattsse, @mablr, @figtracer, @Thomas-Smets.
* **Coverage, state diffs and lints:** `forge coverage --keep-optimizer` keeps optimizer settings. State diffs label EIP-1967 proxy slots, dynamic array elements and ERC-7201 namespaces declared in libraries, and two lints catch colliding namespaces and slots that don't match their namespace (#18445, #18500, #18501, #18028, #18029, #18030) by @DaniPopes, @sakulstra, @mablr, @stevencartavia.
* **Scripts and properties:** `forge script` lists the contracts it deployed, named by `vm.label`, and `forge properties` agents search different focus areas, set with `--focus` (#17971, #18189, #18194) by @aelmanaa, @mablr, @figtracer, @stevencartavia.

### Tempo T14 configurable accounts

* **Cast:** `cast wallet` creates configurable accounts and manages their owners. `send`, `mktx`, `batch-send`, `estimate` and zone transfers sign as configurable accounts with their owners' keys, a configurable account can act as another account's access key, and owners on other machines approve with `cast wallet sign --no-hash`, including `--p256`. `cast tx` shows their signatures (#18378, #18410, #18407, #18506, #18510, #18535, #18507, #18426, #18421, #18508) by @mablr, @stevencartavia.
* **Forge:** cheatcodes derive, digest and sign for configurable accounts, and `forge script` sends as one whose owners sign on other machines (#18408, #18411, #18443) by @mablr.
* **Anvil:** it simulates and impersonates configurable accounts, including forked ones, and traces decode their precompile (#18377, #18536, #18509, #18374, #18372) by @mablr.

### Anvil and Cast

* **Anvil:** `anvil_tempoCreateToken` creates TIP-20 tokens at chosen addresses, and Tempo forks infer their epoch length (#18099, #18020, #18077) by @0xKarl98, @mablr.
* **Cast:** `cast safe` verifies Safe transaction hashes locally, takes `--chain` and rejects a chain ID mismatch, and decodes Safe v1.3.0 events. Errors name an eaten trailing flag or the transaction hash that timed out (#18418, #18425, #17926, #17813) by @0xKarl98, @mablr, @ninglinLiu, @stevencartavia, @aelmanaa.

## Bug fixes

### Execution and Anvil

* **Execution:** fork preflight reads drop `requireCanonical`, so Rootstock forks work (#18486) by @Ynyesto.
* **Anvil:** calls, estimates and replays treat empty accounts as absent, as mining does, and Monad RPCs report the charged gas (#18128, #18513) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @haythemsellami.
* **Anvil RPC and mining:** mining and RPC locks are fixed, reorg blocks differ from the blocks they replace, deep fork rollbacks restore block hashes, Otterscan searches respect the head and keep block order, beacon blob lookups work, and Tempo fork dev accounts get fee tokens. Gas estimation prints console logs only on failure, full DKG is announced before rotation, and transactions below intrinsic or calldata floor gas, legacy transactions for other chains and code over Tempo precompiles are rejected (#16711, #18064, #18239, #18275, #18439, #18014, #18015, #18131, #18135, #18560, #17940, #18069, #18279, #18010, #18100) by @gomesalexandre, @mablr, @stevencartavia, @0xKarl98, @figtracer, @Snan0M, @aelmanaa, @mortezashojaei.

### Cheatcodes and state diffs

* **Cheatcodes:** stale deals are cleared, `expectCreate` ignores failed creates, cheatcode forks use the retry settings, fork-mode access checks the executing code, `writeJson` handles quoted keys and self-referencing structs serialize. Env values are redacted from errors (#18176, #18155, #18074, #18358, #18004, #18466, #17724) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @0xKarl98, @Steven-J-22, @figtracer, @Naveen-6087.
* **State diffs:** accesses are attributed to the right frame and account, and struct members, user-defined value types and proxy storage decode correctly (#18381, #18505, #18147, #18148, #18161, #18496, #18497, #18499) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @sakulstra.

### Fuzzing, invariants and coverage

* **Invariants:** every failed handler assertion is detected with its message, timed campaigns check the initial state, reverts between checks fail every invariant, and `afterInvariant` counterexamples drop an unexecuted call. Shrinking stops at the invariant timeout and keeps its progress (#18158, #18286, #18357, #18455, #18454, #18405, #18414) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @figtracer.
* **Fuzzing:** corpus calls are kept and admitted correctly, the final sync no longer livelocks, the reported failure and `call_override` targets are deterministic, runtime dictionary samples are no longer crowded out by literals, `SUB`-based equality checks give comparison hints, and coverage includes the failing input (#18122, #18137, #18230, #18484, #18123, #18124, #18197, #17989, #18456) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @figtracer, @aelmanaa.
* **Coverage:** failure stubs, `break` and `continue` arms, and source offsets of dynamically linked tests map to the right items, and `require`, ternary, Yul `if`, function and statement anchors match solc under Solar and via-IR (#18094, #18446, #18518, #18528, #18529, #18185, #18447, #18450, #18448, #18516, #18517, #18541, #18563) by @djolertrk, @mablr, @DaniPopes.

### Symbolic execution

* **Forge equivalence:** the engine matches Forge for call depth, halts, `CREATE` limits, EIP-7702, env and expectation cheatcodes, `deal` and nonce writes, `BLOBHASH` and invariants after `setUp`. Counterexamples replay the model's storage, and missing storage layouts are recompiled (#17854, #18120, #18432, #18544, #18299, #18459, #18463, #18462, #18102, #18059, #18136, #18175, #18341, #18344, #18338, #18315, #18355, #18365, #18366, #18367, #18368, #18387, #18388, #18144, #18066, #18090, #18101, #18431, #18440, #18441, #18458, #18582) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @figtracer, @grandizzy, @joshieDo, @emmajam, @pepyakin, @0xKarl98, @mattsse.
* **Solver and normalizer:** common DeFi math now proves instead of timing out, including `mulDiv`, `ceilDiv`, pro-rata shares, vault round trips, divide-first fees and constant-product swaps. Large storage offsets can alias, and keccak, division, remainder and masking facts are decided before the solver (#18057, #18058, #18193, #18342, #18346, #18349, #18350, #18351, #18530, #18531, #18546, #18547, #18548, #18551, #18557, #18559, #18561, #18545, #18169, #18583, #18587, #18591, #18592, #18597, #18598, #18600, #18601, #18595) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @figtracer, @grandizzy, @joshieDo, @emmajam, @pepyakin, @0xKarl98, @clement-ux, @Thomas-Smets.

### Forge, scripts and config

* **Formatter:** `forge fmt` no longer writes unparsable files, `for` loop block styles are respected, unmatched `disable-end` directives are ignored, blank lines no longer make single-line bodies unstable, zero trimming no longer leaves underscores, and default and configured inputs that resolve outside the project root are skipped (#18182, #18393, #18356, #18422, #17509, #18237) by @Thomas-Smets, @mablr, @0xKarl98, @figtracer, @stevencartavia, @erkancamli.
* **Forge:** `forge test --json` stays valid JSON with `live_logs` on and during long fuzz campaigns with edge coverage, `forge test` analyzes all sources, gas snapshot groups can no longer be absolute paths or contain `.` or `..`, `forge create` waits for lagging receipts, and `forge properties` campaigns no longer share session files (#18419, #18383, #18477, #18468, #18232, #18008) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @figtracer, @0xKarl98, @kutluhaneth46.
* **Config:** empty library lists parse, chainless explorer entries get their own cache, unknown `[rpc_endpoints]` and `[etherscan]` keys warn, and `foundry.lock` ends with a newline (#18472, #18487, #17981, #18379) by @unixglo, @mablr, @0xKarl98, @aelmanaa.
* **Scripts:** `--resume` stops at reverts across sequences, a plain `--broadcast` over an unreadable previous export requires `--start-fresh`, several Ledger signers load at once, sponsored estimates include fee payer access, EIP-7702 authorizations survive fee token resolution on Tempo, and prompts work without a terminal (#18149, #18436, #18606, #18404, #18428, #18005) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @Steven-J-22.
* **Traces, debugger and lints:** revert data with control characters shows as hex, constructor runtimes and test linking backtraces resolve, events with struct parameters decode from the signature cache, ERC-7201 labels survive extra compiler profiles, PUSH values show in the debugger, and `reentrancy-events` no longer treats call-free assembly as an external call. `forge init` and `forge install` say when `git` is missing (#17934, #17949, #17904, #18041, #17986, #18115, #18467, #18045) by @aelmanaa, @mablr, @stevencartavia, @PlasticDigits, @figtracer, @Osraka.

### Cast and Chisel

* **Cast:** ENS names resolve only for address arguments, arguments after raw calldata and out-of-range `to-int256` values are rejected, `cast logs` rejects extra topics instead of dropping them, `sig --optimize` no longer wraps the nonce, `decode-event` keeps cached indexed flags, and `cast wallet new` works in unreadable directories. Cast reports an unresolvable project root instead of panicking (#18119, #18252, #18072, #17682, #17755, #17990, #18007, #18586) by @mablr, @0xKarl98, @Snan0M, @clippytool, @stevencartavia, @figtracer, @Ravan002, @aelmanaa, @mattsse.
* **Chisel:** inspection works with Solar and `--ir-minimum`, calls without a return value need no semicolon, and dumps work without source matches (#18199, #18233, #18043, #18201) by @mattsse, @stevencartavia, @rome-xi, @figtracer, @aelmanaa, @mablr.

### Other fixes and chores

* **Fixes to changes made earlier in this release**, mostly from the evm2 migration and the new invariant, symbolic, remapping and configurable-account features (#18332, #18359, #18396, #18363, #18333, #18385, #18549, #18395, #18427, #18164, #18174, #18519, #18112, #18231, #18461, #18406, #18162, #18576, #18537, #18580, #18420, #18570) by @figtracer, @mablr, @stevencartavia, @grandizzy, @joshieDo, @emmajam, @pepyakin, @0xKarl98, @mds1, @haythemsellami.
* **Tests, CI, docs and refactors** (#17894, #18143, #18178, #18187, #18434, #18113, #18114, #18116, #18118, #18228, #18245, #18095, #18502, #18444, #18429, #18542, #18375, #18413, #18061, #17952, #17897, #18097, #18060, #18449, #18521, #18080, #18533, #18539, #18562, #18525, #18522, #18062, #18141, #18150, #18170, #18191, #18370, #18380, #18401, #18403, #18409, #18437, #18534, #18568, #18569, #18584, #18577, #18578) by @0xKarl98, @mablr, @joshieDo, @gakonst, @figtracer, @stevencartavia, @DaniPopes, @aelmanaa, @ninglinLiu, @jenpaff.

## Other behavior changes

* **evm2:** transfers that overflow a balance saturate instead of halting, re-selecting a fork restores its whole block environment, and `vm.setEvmVersion` applies to new calls only. Traces show halted nested calls using all forwarded gas. Anvil removes empty touched accounts (EIP-161), so state roots can differ from 1.9, and rejects EIP-4844 transactions on OP Stack networks (#17541, #18278).
* **Downgrades:** older versions discard fork caches written by 1.10 and cannot load Anvil dumps written with `--preserve-historical-states` (#17541).
* **Tempo T14:** `cast wallet new` creates a configurable account on Tempo chains with T14 active. Pass `--eoa` for a conventional account (#18378, #18410).
* **Invariants:** multi-worker campaigns no longer reserve a worker for selector focus. Use `targetSelector` to target one handler (#18184).
* **Symbolic execution (preview):** soundness fixes turn some previously passing tests into failures with replayed counterexamples (#18057, #18090, #18101, #18175).
* **Lints:** the new ERC-7201 lints run on build and fail builds with `--deny warnings` (#18029, #18030).
* **Rust API:** revm types are gone from `foundry-evm*` and `anvil`, and Anvil's `PrecompileFactory` no longer has `install` (#17541, #18375).

## v1.9.0 (2026-11-02)

**What you get:**

* **SolDB debugger.** `--debug` now runs on [SolDB](https://github.com/walnuthq/soldb) and debugs large tests without exhausting memory. On a 1.46M-step Aave v4 test, peak memory footprint drops from 27.6 GiB to 0.92 GiB and the session opens 5.8× sooner (6.58 s → 1.13 s).
* **Fork reuse.** Creating a fork that already exists reuses it instead of reloading its cache. With a 20 MB fork cache and a local RPC, 40 suites that call `createSelectFork` in `setUp` run 26× faster (5.15 s → 0.20 s).
* **Faster invariant shrinking.** The shrinker drops blocks of calls first and stops once no call can be removed. It finds the same minimal counterexample up to 35× faster (38 s → 1.1 s).
* **Immediate mining in Anvil.** Anvil mines each transaction as it arrives. viem gets its receipt in 2 ms instead of waiting 4 s for its next poll.
* **Lower memory.** Anvil and Cast stream RPC results without building a JSON tree, and coverage counts hits densely. `cast rpc --json` traces use 80% less memory, Anvil traces 52% less and coverage 34% less.
* **New tools.** `forge properties` and `forge exploit`, transient-storage cheatcodes, and Tempo consensus in Anvil.
* **About 190 fixes** across script recovery, cheatcodes, gas accounting, Anvil and symbolic execution.

## Action required

* **Debugger:** `--debug` opens SolDB. The built-in debugger and `--debug-layout` are removed, and `--dump` now writes a SolDB bundle directory instead of a JSON file (#17429).
* **Gas snapshots:** regenerate them for tests that deploy contracts with `new`. Dynamic test linking turns `new` into `vm.deployCode`, which now charges its creation gas (#17732, #18034).
* **`vm.getRecordedLogs`:** it no longer returns logs from calls or creations that revert or halt, including reverts expected with `expectRevert` (#17866).
* **CREATE2 factory:** with `always_use_create_2_factory = true`, salted `vm.deployCode` deploys through the factory. The address changes, and the constructor sees the factory as `msg.sender` (#17471).
* **Anvil:** it mines immediately, so concurrent transactions may land in separate blocks. Pass `--transaction-coalescing-window 5` to restore the 1.8 behavior. Priced calls below the base fee return `-32003` (#17578, #17419).
* **`--resume`:** it fails when a sequence has a recorded revert and operations left to send, including broadcasts from older versions. Pass `--broadcast --start-fresh` to archive the run and broadcast again (#18031, #17736, #17851, #17964).
* **Tempo:** Tempo mainnet activates T13 on 2026-11-03 at 15:00 UTC. Local Tempo nodes that follow the wall clock switch from T12 to T13 at that time (#18021).

## Other behavior changes

* **Script sender:** when `--sender` and a single `--private-key` are both given, the script runs as `--sender`. Before, `msg.sender` came from the key while broadcasts came from `--sender` (#17528).
* **Delegatecall broadcasts:** a `DELEGATECALL` or `CALLCODE` at the broadcast depth is now an error instead of being recorded as a plain `CALL` (#17794).
* **Coverage:** executed bytecode is credited only to exactly matching artifacts, so coverage of code installed with `vm.etch` may drop (#17520).
* **Remappings:** absolute remapping aliases no longer apply inside the project root. For affected projects, bytecode metadata no longer depends on the checkout path and can differ from 1.8 builds (#17507).
* **Gas reporting:** flamegraph and `evm-profile` gas no longer add refunds, and under Amsterdam top-level creates are charged EIP-8037 account-creation state gas (#17728, #17545).
* **Anvil:** block timestamps strictly increase, so bursts of blocks can run ahead of wall-clock time. Slow pubsub clients are disconnected instead of buffered. Reversed `eth_newFilter` ranges, integer `trace_get` indices and unknown trace blocks return errors (#17373, #17909, #17681, #17308, #17777).
* **`vm.writeToml`:** integers above `i64::MAX` are written as strings instead of lossy floats (#18016).
* **Rust API:** callers must use `DebuggerBuilder::run` instead of the removed debugger API (#17429).

## Features

### Forge

* **SolDB debugger:** `--debug` in `forge test`, `forge script`, `cast run` and `cast call` opens an interactive view in a terminal and a `soldb>` prompt otherwise. It reads sources from build info, so files rewritten by dynamic test linking show correct lines, and it restores the terminal if it panics (#17429, #18035, #17960) by @figtracer, @mablr.
* **`forge properties` and `forge exploit`:** `forge properties` runs a swarm of agents you bring yourself, each in an isolated copy of the project, and reports the bugs they prove with failing tests. `forge exploit` asks a model on the Tempo Gateway to find a bug and prove it with a test. Both run generated tests in a restricted sandbox (#17259) by @figtracer.
* **Coverage and mutation testing:** `forge coverage --report gaps` writes every uncovered item as JSON, and mutation testing can replace function bodies with constants (#17183, #17599) by @decofe, @siosw.
* **Linked libraries:** setting `allow_linked_libraries = false` fails builds that need linked libraries (#13585) by @mgiagante.
* **Cheatcodes and state diffs:** added `vm.storeTransient` and `vm.loadTransient`, and state diffs decode ERC-7201 namespaces (#17484, #17869) by @awss1i, @sakulstra.
* **Fuzzing:** the fuzzer reuses whole structs from results, events and views, keeps only applicable comparison hints, and builds its dictionary deterministically (#18017, #17459, #17808, #17931) by @0xalpharush, @figtracer, @stevencartavia.
* **Fork prefetch:** the opt-in `fork_prefetch` setting warms new fork blocks in the background with the keys earlier runs read (#17673) by @figtracer.
* **Warnings:** `forge script` warns when a dry run uses the default sender and while it waits on a pending receipt, and it can unlock a keystore without an address to find the sender. Forge warns when an explicit network does not match a fork (#17839, #17977, #17818, #18037) by @stevencartavia, @aelmanaa, @figtracer.

### Anvil

* **Tempo consensus:** Anvil signs locally mined blocks. Consensus can be configured from the CLI, queried and subscribed to, identities can be rotated, and fork certificates and consensus rounds are forwarded (#17729, #17773, #17799, #17820, #17822, #17867, #17942, #18009, #18033) by @0xKarl98, @mablr.
* **New RPCs and chains:** added `anvil_setMiningPaused`, `anvil_setNextBlockParentBeaconBlockRoot`, 200 ms Base blocks, and CIP-64 transactions with native fees (#17571, #17305, #17128, #17481) by @spalladino, @mattsse, @meyer9, @mablr.
* **Coalescing window:** `--transaction-coalescing-window` batches transactions that arrive together into one block (#17448) by @mablr.

### Cast and editors

* **`cast`:** it decodes indexed event parameters, and 4byte commands check the local signatures cache (#17634, #17919) by @mattsse, @aelmanaa.
* **Editors:** the VS Code extension is on the Marketplace and Open VSX, and the Zed extension downloads Forge when none is installed (#17463, #17858) by @DaniPopes.

## Performance

* **Fork reuse:** `createFork`, `createSelectFork` and `rollFork` reuse an existing fork instead of reloading its cache (#17418, #17739) by @figtracer.
* **Invariant shrinking:** the shrinker drops blocks of calls first and stops once no call can be removed, instead of spending the whole `shrink_run_limit`. Optimization mode keeps removals that raise the score (#17742) by @figtracer.
* **Immediate mining:** Anvil mines each transaction as it arrives again, so clients get receipts without waiting for a poll (#17578) by @figtracer.
* **Memory:** the debugger records steps without a second copy of the trace. Anvil and Cast serialize RPC results without building a JSON tree first, and coverage counts hits densely (#17429, #17650, #17672, #17671) by @figtracer, @DaniPopes.
* **Symbolic execution:** cached context classifications explore the same paths about 3× faster on Halmos `Storage4` (#17701) by @mablr.
* **Build times:** smaller binaries and faster builds from aligned dependency features, trimmed dependency defaults and less monomorphization (#17783, #17806, #17788, #17802, #17787, #17786, #17798) by @DaniPopes.

## Bug fixes

### Scripts

* **Script recovery:** `--resume` no longer sends operations planned after a recorded on-chain revert, and rebroadcasts are refused over an unfinished run or without its snapshot. Resume keeps the saved endpoint, sponsor and fee token. Multichain errors name their chains, every chain is verified, and simulation uses fixed gas limits, the chain's hardfork gas limits and attached blobs (#18031, #17851, #17964, #17736, #17293, #17753, #17758, #17776, #17880, #17881, #17879, #17885, #17886, #17521, #17861, #17792) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @0xKarl98.

### Cheatcodes and testing

* **`vm.deployCode`:** it behaves like a native CREATE. It charges its creation to the caller, forwards the same gas, and enforces the initcode size limit and Amsterdam account-creation state gas (#17732, #18034, #17471) by @stevencartavia, @mablr.
* **Cheatcodes:** fixed raw transaction failures, reverted snapshot journals, delegated EOA nonces, cooled accounts, `vm.blobBaseFee`, access lists before Berlin, delegations before Prague, `mockFunction` under isolation and exact `uint64` values in `vm.writeToml` (#17389, #17425, #17686, #17678, #17677, #17624, #17640, #17458, #18016, #17794) by @stevencartavia, @mablr, @Snan0M.
* **Dynamic test linking:** compiler failures retry natively and unchanged inputs skip the retry. Via-IR stack errors are avoided, sources are reused on expansion, and deleting a file that no preprocessing decision depends on no longer recompiles scripts (#17610, #17622, #17638, #17841, #17933, #18026) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @0xKarl98, @ninglinLiu.
* **Symbolic execution:** it matches Forge for `expectRevert`, `vm.assume` replays, isolated calls, precompiles and `setUp` accounts (#17945, #17907, #17963, #17947, #17976, #17860, #17865, #17821, #17898) by @stevencartavia, @decofe.

### Anvil

* **Timestamps:** default-path block timestamps strictly increase, and the block after `evm_setTime(T)` is mined at `T` (#17373, #18032) by @Lubov66, @mablr.
* **Fees:** the fee mempool is ordered by effective tip, and priced calls below the base fee are rejected (#17882, #17419) by @stevencartavia, @figtracer.
* **Pubsub:** it respects backpressure, no longer drops clients over large responses, and skips blocks removed by revert, rollback or reorg in logs subscriptions (#17909, #17935, #17936) by @0xKarl98, @stevencartavia.
* **Fork and history:** fee state is restored on rollback and reorg, rollback can reach the fork root, head reads and block tags resolve against one snapshot, fork RPC connections are isolated, and fork credentials are redacted from logs and `anvil_nodeInfo` (#17795, #17835, #17347, #17703, #17598, #17704, #17537, #17421, #17908) by @stevencartavia, @0xKarl98, @figtracer.
* **RPC errors:** reversed block ranges in `eth_newFilter` and integer `trace_get` indices are rejected, and unknown trace blocks return not found (#17681, #17308, #17777) by @Ravan002, @mattsse, @banteg.

### Cast and verification

* **`cast`:** `decode-error` and `decode-event --json` output stays valid JSON, cached 4byte signatures with another selector are ignored, `cast call --trace` respects fees, and `cast run` warns when it skips system transactions (#17925, #17939, #17527, #17906, #17946) by @ninglinLiu, @stevencartavia.
* **Solar:** Solar's experimental codegen warning is accepted, and `forge verify-contract` keeps Solar build metadata in the compiler version (#17903, #17890) by @figtracer, @DaniPopes.

## Dependencies

* Solar 0.3.0, with codegen fixes for decoded bytes padding (#17943, #18054)
* Solidity 0.8.38 (#17743) by @figtracer
* Tempo v1.17.0 for T13 activation (#18021) by @grandizzy

## v1.8.7 (2026-10-29)

v1.8.7 is a patch release on top of v1.8.6 that fixes two compile cache regressions introduced in v1.8.4 and picks up dependency security fixes.

## Fixes

* With dynamic test linking enabled (the default), widening a build after a narrower one, for example `forge build --skip script` followed by `forge build`, no longer recompiles every cached source. Only the newly included files are compiled, while tests, scripts, and the sources that depend on them are still invalidated when the build context changes (#17841, foundry-rs/foundry-core#277) by @mablr. Fixes #17836.
* The compile cache is no longer discarded when the project directory moves or is checked out at a different path, because cached remappings are now stored relative to the project root (foundry-rs/foundry-core#274, foundry-rs/foundry-core#279, foundry-rs/foundry-core#288) by @ninglinLiu, @mablr. Fixes #17829.

## Dependencies

* Update foundry-core to `e47676d`, which also includes block explorer, wallet, and fork cache fixes such as honoring explorer API keys from the environment, accepting `ETH_PASSWORD` without `--keystore`, and resolving mixed 0.8 pragmas with Solar.

## Security

* Update `tokio` to 1.53.3, fixing RUSTSEC-2026-0386 (#17775).
* Update `ctutils` to 0.4.5, fixing RUSTSEC-2026-0385 (#17767).
* Update `zstd` to 0.14.3, `zstd-safe` to 8.2.0 and `zstd-sys` to 2.1.2, fixing RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403 and RUSTSEC-2026-0410 (#17838).

## v1.8.5 (2026-10-05)

Foundry v1.8.5 is a focused patch release led by an Anvil mining fix for ready transactions left in the pool after a full block. Previously, burst submissions such as `forge script --broadcast` could stall indefinitely while Forge waited for receipts. It also includes targeted correctness improvements across Forge, Anvil, Cast, symbolic execution, Base, and Tempo.

***

## Highlights

* Kept Anvil mining while ready transactions remain after a full block, for both automine and `evm_mine`. Mining continues only when the previous block made progress, avoiding empty-block loops for transactions that can never fit (#17266) by @stevencartavia.
* Restored Base's seeded genesis state across `anvil_reset` (#17320) by @mattsse.
* Simplified the symbolic executor by removing redundant solver and execution layers while retaining end-to-end and nightly coverage (#17279, #17339) by @figtracer, @mattsse.
* Improved invariant corpus replay by enforcing sender, target, and selector policies, restoring state after rejected replay entries, and validating persisted optimization results before reuse (#17274, #17286, #17292) by @stevencartavia, @figtracer.
* Moved gas-snapshot checking until all test suites complete and kept `forge test --list` from contaminating the build cache (#17318, #17262) by @mattsse, @stevencartavia.
* Aligned Parity trace responses and lookups with their expected wire semantics: replay responses now include `transactionHash`, `trace_get` follows trace addresses, mined traces omit nested precompile calls, and unknown blocks or transactions are reported consistently. Block trace methods now reject `pending`, and raw transaction tracing enforces the code-sender rule (#17301, #17302, #17303, #17304, #17306, #17309) by @mattsse.
* Corrected call fee and gas preparation: fee-free calls run with zero base and blob base fees, cap-only calls pay the base fee, omitted gas is bounded by the sender's allowance, and conflicting fee or input fields are rejected (#17310, #17311, #17312, #17307) by @mattsse.
* `cast interface` now detects verified proxies and generates the implementation interface instead of the proxy shell (#17153) by @sakulstra.
* Fixed `cast decode-tx --json` to emit a JSON object instead of a JSON-encoded string (#17317) by @mattsse.
* Improved Tempo replay and local-node behavior, including standard-envelope execution, gas-schedule preservation, local fee-token resolution, and omitted nonce handling (#17260, #17278, #17327, #17326) by @figtracer, @mattsse.

***

## Compatibility notes

* The public Rust APIs `foundry_evm_symbolic::BUILTIN_SYMBOLIC_SOLVERS` and `EvmOpts::fork_network` were removed as part of the symbolic and shared-EVM simplifications (#17279, #17339).
* `cast interface` now emits the implementation ABI for verified proxies, and `cast decode-tx --json` now returns structured JSON rather than a JSON string (#17153, #17317).
* Malformed values passed to `envOr` now revert instead of using the fallback (#16924).
* Parity trace clients may need to account for the response and lookup changes described above, especially `transactionHash` in replay responses, trace-address indexing in `trace_get`, omitted nested precompile calls, and stricter unknown or `pending` block handling (#17301, #17302, #17303, #17306, #17309).

***

## v1.8.4 (2026-10-01)

Foundry v1.8.4 builds on [v1.8.3](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/releases/tag/v1.8.3) with durable script recovery, native Base execution, external compiler adapters, integrated editor clients, expanded block-access-list and Tempo tooling, and substantial correctness and performance improvements across tracing, compilation, fuzzing, symbolic execution, formatting, linting, and Chisel.

***

## Forge, scripting, and testing

**Script recovery compatibility:** Forge now stores authoritative resume state in a private, versioned `.recovery.json` file under `cache/`. Preserve both `broadcast/` and `cache/` until a deployment is complete. Forge 1.8.4 can import a consistent legacy artifact pair, but older Forge versions must not resume a deployment after 1.8.4 has written generation-tagged recovery state.

* Added crash-safe recovery snapshots, persisted exact signed payloads before submission, and fail-closed handling for ambiguous browser-wallet or unlocked-RPC outcomes. Recovery covers ordinary, multichain, sponsored, and Tempo batch submissions; ambiguous delegated attempts can be resolved explicitly with `--resume-attempt` and either `--resume-tx-hash` or `--resume-retry` (#16993, #16995, #16996, #17023, #17181, #17251) by @stevencartavia.
* Added executable external compiler adapters for EVM projects whose manifests and dependency resolution do not fit Foundry's Solidity source-file model (#16980) by @figtracer.
* Added VS Code and Zed editor clients and a `forge lsp` launcher backed by Forge's embedded Solar language server (#16730) by @0xKarl98.
* Improved dynamic test-linking and compiler-cache correctness for imported constants, cached libraries, filtered builds, import cycles, and native-bytecode fallback. Fallback now tracks transitive import closures instead of invalidating every test and script after any edit (#16908, #17003, #17014, #17211, #17238, #17254) by @mablr, @stevencartavia, @figtracer.
* Added `vm.eth_getProof`, fixed salted `vm.deployCode` broadcasts through CREATE2, and made local EIP-2935 history-storage clearing revertible across calls and snapshots (#17053, #17192, #17194) by @zexoverz, @stevencartavia.
* Improved persisted invariant failure replay, nested handler identity, shrinking, symbolic frontier reporting, and time/block-aware corpus replay (#16850, #16953, #16981, #17099, #17140, #17235) by @figtracer, @kriss39, @stevencartavia.
* Expanded symbolic execution for aliasing addresses, symbolic mock targets, reverting-call cheatcode state, empty precompile accounts, fork-gated opcodes, exceptional halts, and failed `ecrecover` returndata; empty proof domains and unsafe predicate assumptions no longer report vacuous success (#16964, #16965, #16966, #17119, #17132, #17201, #17212, #17217, #17218) by @Bruce039, @0xShadowX, @figtracer.

***

## Networks, Anvil, and tracing

* Added native Base execution across Forge, Cast, Chisel, scripts, and Anvil, including Base hardforks, deposits, EIP-8130 transactions, precompiles, mining, estimation, tracing, transaction-pool ordering, and forks (#16809, #16224) by @mablr, @lukasrosario.
* Added EIP-7928 block access list production in Anvil and used available BAL data to prewarm fork and transaction-hash replay state (#16917, #16956, #17022) by @figtracer, @0xKarl98.
* Fixed Optimism and Base deposit replay, OP fee-context handling, and incompatible cross-family fork execution (#17130, #17197) by @mablr.
* Improved Tempo nonce-lane ordering, sponsored EIP-7702 authority handling, generic RPC replay fidelity, expiry limits, and protocol support (#17139, #17193, #17195, #17241, #17244) by @stevencartavia, @decofe, @mattsse.
* Corrected Parity trace defaults and new-account state diffs, restored VM trace alignment and reverted-CREATE handling, and reduced memory by replaying historical struct logs from parent state instead of retaining mined opcode steps. Block replay now runs once and reports unavailable historical state explicitly (#17078, #17106, #17226, #17240, #17249, #17250) by @mattsse, @banteg, @mablr, @HubertRitzdorf-ChainSecurity, @stevencartavia.
* Fixed snapshot restoration for the transaction pool and pending prevrandao, and pruned historical state discarded by `evm_revert` (#17044, #17184, #17187) by @stevencartavia.
* Aligned `cast run` with Nitro poster-gas and ArbSys accounting and reported the replayed L2 block correctly (#17069, #17093, #17094) by @stevencartavia, @mattsse.

***

## Cast and developer tools

* Added Tempo zone deposit, withdrawal, settlement waiting, and Earn callback encoders, plus TIP-20 role inspection and grant/revoke commands (#16903, #17246) by @mattsse.
* Added `cast bal` / `cast block-access-list` and used BAL prestate to accelerate `cast run` while respecting explicit EVM overrides (#16933, #16931, #17213) by @mattsse, @mablr.
* Added decoded fields to `cast logs` for event declarations, decoded calldata with ERC-8021 suffixes, and improved `cast run` diagnostics and support for unknown chains and ZKsync traces (#16322, #17171, #17090, #17091, #17092, #17095) by @e1Ru1o, @mattsse.
* Decoded canonical dynamic constructor arguments and rejected ambiguous nested encodings instead of silently selecting one match (#16922, #17233) by @kriss39, @figtracer.
* Preserved explicit empty Tempo keychain scopes as deny-all policies, rejected scopes on pre-T3 chains, and listed Turnkey signers through `cast wallet list --turnkey` (#17255, #17169) by @figtracer, @aelmanaa.
* Improved formatter stability for normalized widths and assignments, prevented directory formatting from following symlinks outside the project, and expanded lint analysis for flash-loan repayment loops, sender aliases, unused function values, compound assignments, and duplicate arithmetic writes (#17137, #17205, #17206, #17196, #16628, #16943, #16944, #16974, #17177) by @CalvinTjoaquinn, @mablr, @0xKarl98, @gomesalexandre, @0xShadowX, @Osraka, @wavey0x.
* Removed RPC and explorer credentials from Chisel session caches, isolated `chisel view` from unrelated project setup, and displayed external function references in the REPL (#17143, #17191, #17131) by @0xKarl98, @stevencartavia.

***

## Compatibility notes

* The minimum supported Rust version for source builds is now 1.98 (#17188) by @stevencartavia.
* Alloy 2.5.0 changes `trace_filter` to intersect both address dimensions when both are supplied and rejects malformed `0x00`-tagged legacy envelopes (#17077) by @mattsse.
* Anvil now preserves empty Parity trace-type lists, defaults `trace_callMany` to `latest`, and treats an omitted `trace_filter` range as latest-only (#17078) by @mattsse.
* Historical default struct logs now require replayable parent state; nodes without it return an explicit unavailable-state error (#17240, #17249) by @HubertRitzdorf-ChainSecurity, @stevencartavia.
* Chisel no longer persists endpoint credentials in session files, so older fork sessions may require credentials again when loaded (#17143, #17191) by @0xKarl98.

***

## v1.8.3 (2026-09-15)

Foundry v1.8.3 builds on [v1.8.1](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/releases/tag/v1.8.1) with expanded Glamsterdam support and fixes across fork execution, scripting, cheatcodes, formatting, linting, and Chisel sessions. It also adds Safe and token commands to Cast, expands invariant fuzzing and symbolic follow-up, updates Tempo support through T13, and enables PGO for x86\_64 GNU/Linux release binaries.

Note: v1.8.2 was left unpublished after RUSTSEC-2026-0285 flagged its rustls dependency. The patched binaries ship as v1.8.3.

***

## Forge and configuration

* Fixed nested broadcast nonce tracking under isolation so sender nonces advance when a nested broadcast call is not executed as a separate isolated transaction ([#16853](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16853)) by @mablr.
* Fixed dynamic test linking generating malformed Solidity for parenthesized constructor expressions, including `(new Target){value: 1 ether}()` and calls without options ([#16854](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16854)) by @mablr.
* Added `forge reinit` to force-restore Git submodules to their recorded revisions, discarding local submodule changes, and fixed missing-dependency installation and remapped test dependency handling ([#16508](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16508), [#16722](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16722), [#16686](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16686)) by @figtracer, @decofe, @mablr.
* Added resolved compiler settings to `forge build -vv` and a runtime `--hardfork` override for Forge and Chisel ([#16337](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16337), [#16406](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16406)) by @figtracer, @stevencartavia.
* Fixed custom-layout contract linking, typed enum bindings, compiler restrictions in filtered builds, and Solc executable lookup through `PATH` ([#16488](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16488), [#16379](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16379), [#16530](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16530), [#16494](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16494)) by @stevencartavia, @figtracer, @decofe.
* Fixed script RPC configuration handling, broadcast transaction-hash indexing, and panics when broadcast files and their sensitive caches disagree ([#16589](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16589), [#16715](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16715), [#16580](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16580)) by @mablr, @gomesalexandre.
* Fixed constructor-argument verification for dynamic types and made `verify-bytecode` reject provided constructor arguments that do not match the deployment ([#16569](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16569), [#16056](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16056)) by @gomesalexandre, @mattsse.

***

## Glamsterdam

* Added EIP-8037 state-gas reporting through `Vm.Gas.gasStateUsed` and documented regular gas, state gas, reservoir spillover, refunds, and isolation semantics ([#16387](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16387), [#16772](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16772)) by @figtracer, @mattsse.
* Preserved gas snapshot measurements when separating state gas and post-refund last-frame snapshots for isolated calls, and preserved Amsterdam's state-gas reservoir across isolated execution with transaction gas limits enabled ([#16442](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16442), [#16490](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16490), [#16604](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16604)) by @figtracer.
* Added `vm.getSlotNumber()` and `vm.rollSlot(uint64)` for Amsterdam's EIP-7843 block slot number ([#16784](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16784)) by @mattsse.
* Included the computed EIP-7928 block access list hash in Amsterdam `eth_simulateV1` block headers ([#16673](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16673)) by @mattsse.

***

## Testing, fuzzing, and cheatcodes

**Gas snapshot compatibility:** Whole-test `forge snapshot` totals for isolated tests involving refunds can change due to updated execution gas accounting. Review these differences before regenerating affected baselines.

* Preserved post-refund measurements in isolated `startSnapshotGas` / `stopSnapshotGas` regions, including refunding calls and contract creation ([#16864](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16864)) by @figtracer.
* Fixed exact revert-data matching and required four-byte prefixes for partial revert matches ([#16428](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16428), [#16446](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16446)) by @figtracer, @mattsse.
* Fixed false differences in zero-gas snapshot tolerance checks ([#16565](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16565)) by @gomesalexandre.
* Added additional secp256k1 arithmetic operations ([#16381](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16381)) by @StackOverflowExcept1on.
* Enforced filesystem permissions for `dumpState`, protected `foundry.toml` from `vm.removeDir`, and fixed `expectSafeMemory` panics on short calldata ([#16513](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16513), [#16542](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16542), [#16576](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16576)) by @DicksonWu654, @gomesalexandre.
* Enforced the active protocol initcode-size limit in `vm.executeTransaction`, including when contract-size checks are disabled ([#16551](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16551), [#16590](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16590)) by @mablr, @decofe.
* Separated corpus paths for overloaded fuzz tests, excluded skipped corpus inputs, and preserved useful invariant corpus entries ([#16307](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16307), [#16365](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16365), [#16837](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16837)) by @stevencartavia, @figtracer.
* Added opt-in stateful branch-frontier artifacts and targeted symbolic follow-up that feeds concretely confirmed branch-flipping and invariant-failing sequences back into the corpus ([#16614](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16614), [#16823](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16823)) by @figtracer.
* Fixed symbolic memory-backed array handling, deferred call-branch retries, and enforcement of path limits across symbolic-size forks and nested call completions ([#16747](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16747), [#16800](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16800), [#16825](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16825), [#16848](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16848)) by @figtracer, @gomesalexandre, @mablr.
* Aligned symbolic `expectCall`, `expectRevert`, `mockCall`, and `vm.isContext` behavior with concrete Forge execution ([#16579](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16579), [#16668](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16668), [#16660](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16660), [#16735](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16735), [#16743](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16743)) by @gomesalexandre.
* Fixed coverage tracking for both Yul branch outcomes and line attribution before branch bodies ([#16835](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16835), [#16836](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16836)) by @decofe, @figtracer.

***

## Formatting and linting

* Fixed comment preservation and formatting stability around for-loop headers, constructors, modifiers, tuples, mappings, and binary assignments ([#16648](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16648), [#16787](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16787), [#16786](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16786), [#16840](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16840)) by @gomesalexandre, @figtracer.
* Preserved CRLF lines inside disabled formatting regions and stabilized multiline comment formatting ([#16806](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16806), [#16808](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16808)) by @figtracer.
* Changed the default lint selection to high, medium, and low severities, and excluded configured test and script directories while retaining selected unsafe-cheatcode diagnostics ([#16622](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16622), [#16663](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16663)) by @figtracer.
* Added environment-capture warnings and opt-in reporting of unused inline suppressions with `--report-unused-suppressions` ([#16755](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16755), [#16841](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16841)) by @decofe, @Jorge-Polanco-Roque.
* Improved detection of returned storage mutations and storage-pointer aliases, and removed false positives for internal unused returns, defaulted loop counters, and single-bit mask shifts ([#16475](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16475), [#16582](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16582), [#16813](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16813), [#16667](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16667), [#16710](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16710)) by @stevencartavia, @gomesalexandre, @mablr, @figtracer.

***

## Networks, Anvil, and forking

* Bounded optional fork identity probes to 500 ms per request to prevent stalled RPC gateways from delaying startup ([#16833](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16833)) by @mattsse.
* Preserved Arbitrum L1 `block.number` semantics during local execution while keeping RPC and ArbSys block numbers on L2; fixed Arbitrum transaction, receipt, and blob-environment handling ([#16771](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16771), [#16465](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16465), [#16514](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16514)) by @mablr, @mattsse, @figtracer.
* Updated Tempo support through T13, including current keychain authorization detection and standard EVM halt reasons ([#16717](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16717), [#16779](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16779)) by @decofe.
* Fixed Tempo fork account-state loading to avoid placeholder native balances and incorrect gas usage, including historical reads and downstream forks ([#16811](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16811)) by @mablr.
* Fixed Optimism fee handling for calls and blob transactions, and Celo replay support for CIP-64 transactions and the transfer precompile ([#16507](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16507), [#16519](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16519), [#16500](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16500), [#16512](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16512)) by @stevencartavia, @figtracer, @mablr, @DicksonWu654.
* Added `--fork-state-by-number` for RPC providers without state-by-hash support and `--no-fork-node-info` to skip fork identity probes ([#16774](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16774), [#16778](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16778)) by @dkatzan, @andreyobruchkov.
* Kept forked `trace_call` and `trace_blockOpcodeGas` requests from drifting to the upstream tip, and applied consistent fork-boundary rules to block and transaction queries ([#16733](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16733), [#16732](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16732), [#16720](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16720)) by @gomesalexandre.
* Fixed pending-block query crashes, pending receipt responses, queued transaction replacement, and snapshot time-offset restoration ([#16714](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16714), [#16573](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16573), [#16638](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16638), [#16540](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16540)) by @gomesalexandre, @stevencartavia.
* Fixed fee-history percentile handling, zero-count and zero-gas-limit cases, and validation of future or reversed log ranges ([#16538](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16538), [#16539](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16539), [#16611](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16611), [#16644](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16644), [#16596](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16596), [#16598](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16598)) by @stevencartavia, @gomesalexandre.
* Fixed blob transaction simulation stack overflows, applied genesis headers, and included simulated block sizes ([#16486](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16486), [#16623](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16623), [#16625](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16625)) by @figtracer, @stevencartavia.

## Cast and wallets

* Added Safe account deployment, delegate management, transaction proposals, simulation, signing, and execution commands ([#16377](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16377)) by @decofe.
* Added ERC-4626 vault commands and inspection, plus an ERC-2612 permit helper ([#16601](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16601), [#16605](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16605), [#16672](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16672)) by @mattsse.

* Fixed mined-transaction replay and HyperEVM system-transaction handling, and aligned transaction network selection with configuration and RPC discovery ([#16457](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16457), [#16451](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16451), [#16790](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16790)) by @mattsse, @mablr.
* Preserved explicit transaction types when sending through browser wallets and added support for piped keystore input and named accounts in the default keystore ([#16827](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16827), [#16528](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16528), [#16219](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16219)) by @figtracer, @mablr, @riba2534.
* Fixed multi-recipient session-scope parsing, gaps in `vaddr watch` transfer detection, and negative-number formatting in `from-wei` and `format-units` ([#16688](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16688), [#16716](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16716), [#16646](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16646)) by @gomesalexandre.

## Chisel

* Rejected session IDs that escape the cache directory or address NTFS alternate data streams, and fixed stale session IDs and autosave collisions after deletion or rename ([#16689](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16689), [#16707](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16707), [#16697](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16697), [#16687](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16687)) by @gomesalexandre, @Aditya-9-6.
* Fixed Solidity prelude-file handling and cleared persisted `--force` behavior when loading sessions ([#16510](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16510), [#16511](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16511)) by @DicksonWu654.

## v1.8.1 (2026-08-28)

Foundry v1.8.1 is a patch release on top of [v1.8.0](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/releases/tag/v1.8.0) that fixes regressions in dynamic test linking, Polygon PoS forks, npm remapping auto-detection, linting, and fork endpoint discovery. It also removes the project trust warnings introduced in v1.8.0.

***

## Forge and configuration

* Fixed dynamically linked contract creation so one-shot pranks are consumed correctly and the pranked `tx.origin` is preserved ([#16431](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16431)) by @figtracer.
* Fixed auto-detected remappings for scoped npm dependencies that mix nested and hoisted packages, preventing a nested package from shadowing its hoisted siblings ([#16434](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16434)) by @figtracer.
* Fixed `forge lint` and post-build lint import resolution when `--root` points to a project outside the process working directory ([#16423](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16423)) by @figtracer.
* Fixed inline lint directives and ignored paths for findings reported in inherited or recursively analyzed source files ([#16437](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16437)) by @stevencartavia.

***

## Anvil and forking

* Fixed post-Cancun calls on Polygon PoS and Amoy forks whose Bor headers intentionally omit Ethereum blob gas fields ([#16432](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16432)) by @figtracer.
* Made the initial `anvil_nodeInfo` capability probe optional, allowing non-Anvil fork endpoints with vendor-specific rejection codes to fall back to standard RPC discovery. Once an endpoint is identified as Anvil, later probe failures remain strict ([#16425](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16425)) by @mattsse.

***

## CLI

* Removed the warnings shown before loading project dotenv files or running project-configured local Solc and Vyper executables. Their underlying behavior is unchanged ([#16426](https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/pull/16426)) by @figtracer.

***
